Mollify

MOL-ih-fye · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To mollify appease someone's anger or anxiety.

The airline offered free upgrades to mollify the passengers stranded overnight by the canceled flight.

Worked Example

Nothing the babysitter tried could mollify the toddler after his tower of blocks collapsed.

The toddler is genuinely, specifically angry/upset, and every attempt is aimed at calming that anger -- exactly what mollify describes.

How Mollify Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

appease

appease: calm by giving in to demands

pacify

pacify: bring to a calm, peaceful state

Antonyms

provoke

provoke: stir up anger deliberately

incense

incense: make furiously angry

How Strong Is It? — calm → pacify → mollify

calm vs. mollify

calm vs. mollify: To calm someone is a general, mild effect; to mollify them is to specifically ease their anger, often with a concession.

pacify vs. mollify

pacify vs. mollify: Pacify pushes further than mollify, sometimes implying a more complete, lasting peace rather than just easing the immediate anger.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — molli

root — molli: soft (Latin (mollis))

suffix — -fy

suffix — -fy: to make (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: The root molli- ('soft,' from Latin mollis) plus the verb-forming -fy gives 'to make soft' -- to mollify anger is to soften it.

Use the root in a new word: mollusk

Use the root in a new word: mollusk: Mollusk (a soft-bodied animal like a snail or clam) comes from the same Latin mollis, 'soft,' as mollify.

Root Check

Word Choice

Mollify names the everyday version of appeasement -- calming a specific person's real, immediate anger, usually with an apology or concession. Compare Propitiate (this same unit), which carries a more formal or ceremonial register.
